name: High-Protein Cheeseburger Pasta
intro_html: Think of the boxed hamburger dinner you grew up on, then give it a protein makeover. Lean beef, high-protein penne, real marinara, and melty mozzarella come together into a comfort-food bowl that packs 38 grams of protein for about $2.53 (at everyday cost). Kids inhale it and the macros still behave.
ingredients_display: 93/7 Ground Beef (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Marinara Sauce (Great Value): about 3.5 cups (most of two 24 oz jars) (861 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
Yellow Onion: onion powder/fresh onion in most versions (250 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_closing_html: That is about $2.53 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a from-scratch, high-protein version of a dinner that used to come from a blue box. Catch the beef on sale and it dips even lower.
shop_smart: Protein pasta does real work. The Protein Plus line adds several grams of protein per serving over regular pasta for about the same price. Regular penne works too if you want it cheaper.
Buy the beef on sale and freeze. Same rule as always. Lean beef on sale, split into one-pound packs, frozen. Your batches get cheaper for free.
Store-brand sauce is plenty. A store-brand traditional or marinara sauce is a dollar or two under the name brands and nobody at the table will know.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne to al dente per the box, then drain.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up. Drain any excess fat.
Pour the pasta sauce into the beef and simmer a couple of minutes until hot.
Add the drained penne and stir until every piece is coated.
Fold in the shredded mozzarella off the heat so it turns gooey.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total food weight by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near 415 calories and 38 grams of protein.
upsell_html: High-protein dinners for about $2.53 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.
